call_overview.title: About the call
call_overview.question: What does the call offer, and who can apply?

cards.title: What the call wants
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop, and which problem or need must it address?
cards.answer:
Scholarships for individual students to spend a six-month exchange semester at NTNU learning digital skills for wind and energy systems.
The call is a cascade call (an EU-funded project passing part of its grant on to others) by NTNU, the Norwegian University of Science and Technology in Trondheim, within DigiWind (Digital Masters of Wind and Energy Systems, a Digital Europe Programme project of five universities and four companies that funds advanced digital education in wind and energy systems). It funds no project: it pays a stipend so that students can follow courses in the M.Sc. Electric Power Engineering or M.Sc. Marine Technology programmes. Each student must take 30 credits (about four courses), of which at least two designated DigiWind courses and at least one Electric Power Engineering course. The need behind it is Europe's shortage of engineers with digital skills for the energy transition.
cards.sources:
DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · Programme Overview
Funding & Tenders Portal cascade call page DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 – Spring & Autumn 2027 · NTNU Open Call 2 Offer

cards.title: Project impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
More engineers in Europe who combine power-system or marine engineering with digital skills for wind and energy systems.
DigiWind's stated aim is to equip Europe's top talent with advanced digital skills to drive innovation in wind and energy systems and build a skilled workforce for the green transition. Scholarship holders must also take part in student ambassador activities. The call sets no quantified targets beyond up to 15 scholarships.

cards.title: Who it suits
cards.question: Who may lead, which partners must take part, and how must the work be shared?
cards.answer:
Individual students only, not organisations: final-year bachelor's students or master's students in a relevant engineering field.
- Status: enrolled in a bachelor's or master's degree at a university with an active NTNU exchange agreement
- Background: last-year B.Sc. in Engineering, B.Eng. or B.Sc. in Natural Science, or current M.Sc. students, with a background relevant to electric power engineering or marine technology
- Nationality: passport of an EU/EEA country or of a Digital Europe Programme associated country
- English: IELTS Academic 6.5, TOEFL iBT 88 or Cambridge C1/C2 180, unless a native speaker
There is no consortium. The call suits engineering students, for example at Dutch technical universities with an NTNU exchange agreement.

call_overview.title: Relevance to TenneT
call_overview.question: Why is this call relevant to TenneT?

cards.title: Why it matters to TenneT
cards.question: Why does this call matter to TenneT, and why can't TenneT take part itself?
cards.answer:
It trains future power and offshore engineers in grid digitalisation, a pool TenneT recruits from; TenneT cannot take part because only individual students may apply.
The eligible programmes, electric power engineering and marine technology, match the skills TenneT needs for offshore grid connections and digital grid operation, such as the 2GW Program and the Digital Twin Programme. TenneT could point Dutch students or young recruits to the call, or use it to build contacts with DigiWind partners such as Delft University of Technology. The call sets out no route for an organisation: the scholarship goes to the student.
cards.sources: DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · Who Can Apply?; Programme Overview

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
Up to 15 scholarships of EUR 6,940 each, EUR 104,100 in total, shared between the Spring and Autumn 2027 semesters.
- Grant request: a fixed stipend of EUR 6,940 per student for living and subsistence costs during the six-month exchange
- Funding form: fixed stipend, possibly paid through cash cards from NTNU's Unit for International Relations, after the mobility agreement is signed and enrolment confirmed
cards.sources:
Funding & Tenders Portal cascade call page DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 – Spring & Autumn 2027 · NTNU Open Call 2 Offer; Budget
DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · What's offered

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
The stipend is a fixed amount; students pay the remaining costs themselves.
- Co-financing conditions: tuition is waived for students from NTNU partner universities; each student must personally pay a welfare fee of about EUR 70 per semester
cards.sources: Funding & Tenders Portal cascade call page DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 – Spring & Autumn 2027 · NTNU Open Call 2 Offer

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One application on the F6S platform per round; the Spring 2027 round has closed and the Autumn 2027 round is open.
- Spring 2027 round: closed on 2 November 2026, 17:00 CET
- Autumn 2027 round: 1 March 2027, 17:00 CET; funded from what remains after the Spring round, so fewer places may be left
- Additional procedure: selected students are then enrolled by NTNU as international placement students
cards.sources:
DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · Spring 2027; Autumn 2027; How to apply
Funding & Tenders Portal cascade call page DigiWind NTNU Open Call 2 – Spring & Autumn 2027 · Call interdependency

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
A six-month exchange semester starting 23 August 2027 for the Autumn round.
- Maximum duration: 6 months
- Required start: 23 August 2027 (Autumn 2027); the Spring semester started 11 January 2027
cards.sources: DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · Autumn 2027 timeline

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
Autumn results on 15 March 2027, then enrolment from 1 June to 20 August 2027.
- Expected assessment result: evaluation 2–12 March 2027, results 15 March 2027
- Conditions before starting: accept the offer by email and sign the Declaration of Honour within five business days; enrol at NTNU
cards.sources: DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · Autumn 2027 timeline; Programme Enrolment

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
An F6S application with degree awards, transcripts, CV, personal statement and proof of English.
- Application form: online on F6S
- Partner documents: if selected, a Declaration of Honour and a Learner Agreement
cards.sources: DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · How to apply

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Three NTNU academics score eligible applicants on merit; at least 70% is needed.
- Evaluation criteria and weighting: relevant qualifications 65%; positive mindset towards the green-digital energy transition 25%; commitment to diversity, equality and gender balance 10%
- Thresholds: 70% overall
cards.sources: DigiWind web page NTNU Open Call 2 · Evaluation
